Playback Statistics API for WebAudio

MDN URL

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

@padenot

WebKit standards-position

No response

Other information

There is currently no way to detect whether WebAudio playback has glitches (gaps in the played audio, which typically happens due to underperformance in the audio pipeline). There is an existing way to measure the instantaneous playback latency using AudioContext.outputLatency, but no simple way to measure average/minimum/maximum latency over time. With this API, we want to propose a way to be able to measure the delay of that audio and the playback quality of the audio.

This is a similar request to #527 where we adopted a blanket positive position for all phase 3 TC39 proposals.

The WebAssembly CG (in the W3C) has a phase process for standardization similar (but not identical) to TC39. The SpiderMonkey team reviews all the active proposals in the process, and we only allow proposals that we are positive on to advance to phase 3 (the implementation phase).

Generally most wasm proposals don't have an impact on the larger web platform (e.g. a new arithmetic instruction) and don't need wider review. It'd be nice to have a blanket policy for them. There are some though that have a platform impact and may need a dedicated standards-position.

Specification title

css-pseudo

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#CSSPseudoElement-interface

Explainer URL (if available)

No response

Proposal author(s)

No response

MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSSPseudoElement

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

No response

Other information

With all the new resolutions, here is a new functionality of CSSPseudoElement:

CSSPseudoElement has the following:

  • The type attribute is a string representing the type of the pseudo-element.
  • The element attribute is the ultimate originating element of the pseudo-element.
  • The parent attribute is the originating element of the pseudo-element (Either Element of CSSPseudoElement for nested pseudo-elements).
  • The pseudo(type) method to retrieve nested pseudo-elements.

CSSPseudoElement supports GeometryUtils, meaning it has getBoxQuads(), convertQuadFromNode(), convertRectFromNode(), convertPointFromNode().

Specific events are now also extended to have .pseudoTarget that is either CSSPseudoElement (if interaction has been with pseudo-element) or null. This allows to have more specific information on the event origin, e.g. that not just ultimate originating element (Event.target) has been clicked, but more specifically that it was ::after. Note that the Event.target is unchanged so event only has extra info on pseudo-element interaction.

The events are MouseEvent, PointerEvent, FocusEvent, AnimationEvent, TransitionEvent, KeyboardEvent, TouchEvent.
items.title: CSSPseudoElement interface

Other information

This proposal adds an ai-disclosure global HTML attribute for declaring AI involvement at element-level granularity, complementing the page-level <meta> tag discussed in whatwg/html#9479 and the HTTP-level IETF AI-Disclosure header.

Four values aligned with the IETF header and IPTC Digital Source Type vocabulary: none, ai-assisted, ai-generated, autonomous.

Motivated by the EU AI Act Article 50 (effective August 2026), which requires machine-readable marking of AI-generated text, and by 42+ comments on whatwg/html#9479 requesting element-level granularity that a page-level meta tag cannot provide.

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#597

Other information

Allows callers to specify a maxAge in seconds when setting a cookie with the Cookie Store API.

Currently, developers can use the expires attribute when setting a cookie with the Cookie Store API to set an absolute timestamp for expiry. This can be unintuitive and is impacted by client-side clock skew. RFC6265bis and the document.cookie API provide a Max-Age attribute, which allows for relative cookie lifetimes and ergonomic deletion.
We should provide a maxAge option in the Cookie Store API to support relative expiry and align with these APIs.

Additional relevant discussion: whatwg/cookiestore#293

Specification title

Filter Effects 2: progressive blur via linear-blur()

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

w3c/csswg-drafts#13285

Explainer URL (if available)

No response

Proposal author(s)

@damian-dp

MDN URL

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#595

Other information

Requesting a position on a proposed, backwards-compatible addition to CSS Filter Effects to support progressive (gradient) blur — blur radius that varies spatially across an element (common for toolbar/footer scrims, bottom sheets, "fade-to-blur" overlays, tilt-shift effects).

CSSWG issue (full proposal + use cases + examples):
w3c/csswg-drafts#13285

Proposed API: linear-blur()

A new filter function modelled on linear-gradient() syntax:

filter: linear-blur([<angle> | to <side-or-corner>]?, <blur-stop-list>);
backdrop-filter: linear-blur([<angle> | to <side-or-corner>]?, <blur-stop-list>);

Where <blur-stop-list> follows the same pattern as gradient colour stops (blur value + optional position).

Examples:

/* Simple scrim */
.scrim {
  backdrop-filter: linear-blur(0px, 24px);
}

/* With stop positions */
.scrim {
  backdrop-filter: linear-blur(to bottom, 0px 0%, 0px 50%, 24px 100%);
}

/* Tilt-shift effect */
.tilt-shift {
  filter: linear-blur(to bottom, 8px, 0px 40%, 0px 60%, 8px);
}

Key semantics

This is spatially-varying blur, not blended output. The blur radius at each point is interpolated between stops — the convolution kernel size varies spatially. This is distinct from the existing workaround (backdrop-filter: blur() + mask-image) which blends between unblurred and uniformly-blurred output.

Implementation considerations: True spatially-varying blur is more expensive than uniform blur. Implementations may use approximations (mipmap-based, multi-pass, etc.) provided the visual result preserves detail in low-blur regions consistent with spatially-varying kernel sizes.

Why a new function?

  • Avoids overloading blur() parsing/semantics
  • Reuses the well-known gradient mental model
  • Creates a clear family for future variants (radial-blur(), conic-blur())

This is early-stage (no spec PR yet). Seeking implementer feedback on feasibility/performance and whether implementers would be supportive to this direction.
items.title: Filter Effects 2: progressive blur via `linear-blur()`
